models.model_label: Firm-specific working-capital accrual estimation model (Equation 5; Table 3 Panel A)
models.sample_description: Compustat annual industrial and research firm-years from 1987–1999. The retained specification is estimated separately for each firm; each firm needs at least eight annual observations and past/future CFO data. Table 3 Panel A summarizes 1,725 firm fits, corresponding to 15,234 aggregate firm-year observations; the number of observations varies across firm-specific fits.
models.method_details: The paper identifies a firm-level time-series regression but does not state the underlying estimator used for the individual fits.
models.equation_text: ΔWC_t = b_0 + b_1 CFO_{t−1} + b_2 CFO_t + b_3 CFO_{t+1} + ε_t

fixed_effects.details: The model is fit separately by firm; this grouping is not a reported fixed effect.

standard_errors.details: Table 3 Panel A reports t-statistics for the cross-firm means of firm-specific coefficients, based on the distribution of the 1,725 firm-level estimates. The source does not report the individual-fit standard-error correction.

evidence.quote: The t-statistics in Panel A are determined based on the distribution of the 1,725 coefficients obtained from the firm-specific regressions requiring a minimum of eight observations per firm.
Finally, we add an intercept to Expression (5) to capture possible nonzero average accruals (e.g., average positive working capital accruals due to firm growth).

estimation_procedure.description: Estimate a separate firm-level time-series regression for each firm. Each firm requires at least eight annual observations. The standard deviation of the residuals from each fitted regression is the firm-level accrual-quality measure. Table 3 Panel A summarizes coefficient distributions across 1,725 firms; its t-statistics are based on those cross-firm coefficient distributions.

evidence.quote: To derive practical measures of working capital accrual quality, we use the following firm-level time-series regression:
The residuals from the regression reflect the accruals that are unrelated to cash flow realizations, and the standard deviation of these residuals is a firm-level measure of accrual quality
In addition, we require at least eight years of data to estimate firm-specific regressions.
The t-statistics in Panel A are determined based on the distribution of the 1,725 coefficients obtained from the firm-specific regressions requiring a minimum of eight observations per firm.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
III. SAMPLE SELECTION, DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS,

AND CALIBRATION TESTS
Table 1 summarizes our sample selection. Our sample is obtained from the Compustat
annual industrial and research files over 1987 to 1999. Given Collins and Hribar’s (2002)
result that the balance-sheet approach to deriving CFO leads to noisy and biased estimates,
we use CFO as given in the Statement of Cash Flows reported under the Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards No. 95 (SFAS No. 95, FASB 1987). <sup>3</sup> The sample is restricted to firms with complete data for assets, earnings, cash flow from operations, changes
in accounts receivable, and changes in inventory. The last two requirements ensure sample
firms have significant working capital accruals. Truncating the most extreme 1 percent of
cash from operations, earnings, and changes in working capital, and requiring at least one

McNichols 1998). We do not pursue an industry-specific analysis because the cross-industry variation in the
magnitude of estimation errors is likely to be larger than the typical within-industry variation, and because our
interest is in more generalizable results.
